guide.title: Leave-group-out and low-rank model updates
guide.summary: exact solved models on LIN-001 / LIN-002 states: leave-one-group-out from the total minus each group's state (CPU Bareiss, or every (group, prime) on CUDA with exact CRT and verification), Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury updates with the exact denominator det(I + V^T A^-1 U) and a declared rebuild-or-fail contract when it is zero, row deletions and insertions, ridge changes, subtraction of compatible group states, and a binary64 variant with a certified error bound and condition estimate that refuses when the bound fails.

LIN-003.cpu: Native C (math_linupd.c): immutable exact solved models of LIN-002's normal equations of a fit of a LIN-001 moment state (value units, exact ridge on the features, feature subsets; A, A0, b, y^T y, sum y, n, the design) or of any square rational system, with LIN-002's canonical verified solution set (unique / family with the canonical nullspace / none with a certificate) and statistics, and (on request) A^-1 and det(A) from fraction-free Gauss-Jordan elimination of [M | diag(L) | c] over big integers with A A^-1 = I verified exactly. Exact Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury updates A + U V^T (rank <= 64): the capacitance K = I + V^T A^-1 U and its determinant (rank one: 1 + v^T A^-1 u) formed exactly, det(K) != 0 giving A'^-1 and x' (verified A' x' = b'), det(K) = 0 or no kept inverse following the declared contract (an exact rebuild with LIN-002's canonical singular solution set, or SingularError); row deletions and insertions (U = -/+ Z^T, V = Z^T, y^T y, sum y, n updated; one row: 1 -/+ h), ridge changes (the rank-p Woodbury update or a rebuild from A0, equal), subtraction or addition of a compatible group state. Leave-one-group-out plans: the group states copied, their 192-bit total and every complement total - g formed exactly, the exact integer complement systems (row scaling den 10^(s_u + T)) with their Hadamard bounds; every system solved exactly (LIN-002's Bareiss), or finished from modular residues: agreeing primes, Garner CRT of the det-scaled reduced row echelon form, exact verification against the integer system, more primes when short. A binary64 variant: Gauss-Jordan with partial pivoting on the midpoint of A's tight enclosure, certified by interval arithmetic (alpha >= ||I - R A||_inf, bound = ||R (b - A x~)||_inf / (1 - alpha), kappa >= ||A|| ||R||), refused when alpha >= 1 or the bound exceeds the tolerance.
LIN-003.gpu: CUDA kernel math_linupd_gpu.cu (tr_mgpu_linupd_logo): batched leave-one-group-out solves, one work item per (group, prime in [2^61, 2^62)): the complement normal system of its group formed modulo its prime directly from the copied group states and their total (192-bit words reduced, row scaling and ridge modulo p), then LIN-002's modular Gauss-Jordan elimination (tr_lin_modular_rref) into its own output block (header and det-scaled reduced row echelon form); one output slot per work item, equal bit for bit to the CPU reference tr_linupd_logo_residues (emulated with a scrambled thread order in the tests); the host finish (prime choice, CRT within the Hadamard bounds, exact verification) gives the same canonical models as the CPU path.
budgets: Fit / system: variables = n (<= 63), tensor = n (2n + 1), output = n (n + 1), plus LIN-002's normal-equation needs k (k + 1); updates: tensor = n r + r^2 + n^2 (r <= 64), output = n (n + 1).

Leave-one-group-out plan: states = groups x slots, tensor = systems x n (n + 1), output = systems, bytes = the copies; each system as a fit; CUDA: tensor = systems x primes x (4 + n (n + 1)), bytes = the device copies and residues (at most 1024 primes).
Floating variant: tensor = n^2, bytes = 48 n^2; refused with NotConvergedError when a pivot vanishes, alpha >= 1 or the certified bound exceeds tol.
limitations: Woodbury updates use canonical big rationals (O(n^2 r) rational operations, a gcd each): in the benchmark (20,000 rows) a one-row Woodbury deletion took 2.4 to 14 times as long as the exact rebuild of the updated normal equations with its inverse (3 to 17 unknowns) and was faster than the complete reconstruction from the rows only for small systems (5x at 3 unknowns, within 10% at 9 and 17); a ridge change touching every feature was 3 to 5 times slower than its rebuild from A0. A fraction-free (adjugate) inverse representation that would avoid most gcds is not implemented.
Leave-group-out subtracts moment states and solves each complement system again; there is no low-rank downdate from Gram matrices (moment states do not keep the rows).
Row deletions need the deleted rows and cannot detect rows that were never in the data; rows updates are for common-listwise regression models only.

The CUDA kernel covers the modular LOGO eliminations; the host forms the exact integer systems (Hadamard bounds, verification) and runs the CRT, comparable in cost to the exact CPU solve; updates and the floating variant are CPU code.

No FND-007 certificate is emitted: FND-007's claim kinds are row relations of a scope or polynomial laws, and a fitted model proves neither; every exact solution is verified natively (A x = b, A A^-1 = I, the CRT reconstruction against the integer system) and flagged so.
